topic: An uncaught CORRUPTED_DATA exception from resolveByExactGet or putIfAbsentControlled
canonical_claim: An uncaught `CORRUPTED_DATA` exception from `resolveByExactGet` or `putIfAbsentControlled` in `flushRefBatch` can leave `rt->leader_active` set and `rt->cv` unnotified, wedging the namespace's ref mutation path until restart. An uncaught `CORRUPTED_DATA` from `resolveByExactGet` or `putIfAbsentControlled` in `flushRefBatch` can leave `leader_active` set and waiters blocked indefinitely; the remaining queue must be completed with the exception and notified.; When `flushRefBatch` catches a `CORRUPTED_DATA` exception, it must complete pending and carved survivor requests with that exception, reset `rt->leader_active`, notify `rt->cv`, keep the wedge on corruption, and rethrow.

topic: The all-tree part-files design stores txn_version.txt, metadata_version.txt, and
canonical_claim: The all-tree part-files design stores txn_version.txt, metadata_version.txt, and uuid.txt as ordinary entries in the part manifest rather than a separate ref sidecar. After the all-tree part-files migration, `uuid.txt`, `txn_version.txt`, and `metadata_version.txt` are ordinary manifest entries and no longer populate `RootRef.mutable_files`. The former `RefSidecar` and mutable-per-part-file classification are deleted; `uuid.txt`, `txn_version.txt`, and `metadata_version.txt` are ordinary manifest entries. A CAS manifest is an immutable full file tree whose entries reference blobs or inline bytes; small per-part files such as `uuid.txt` and `checksums.txt` are inline tree entries rather than separate objects.

topic: A precommit may name only a manifest minted
canonical_claim: A precommit may name only a manifest minted by the transaction or the ref's current committed manifest; granting fresh ownership to a foreign manifest id is rejected to prevent ABA reuse. `precommitAdd` may take an unowned `ManifestId` only from the transaction that freshly staged it; already-committed idempotence remains a read-only no-op, making exact `ManifestRef` equality an ABA barrier. `precommitAdd` may introduce an unowned `ManifestId` only when the same transaction freshly staged it, except that the idempotent already-committed-to-this-exact-ref path remains legal.

topic: The new ShardCoverage fields are has_live_precommit, min_live_precommit_writer_epoch, and
canonical_claim: The new `ShardCoverage` fields are `has_live_precommit`, `min_live_precommit_writer_epoch`, and `min_live_precommit_build_sequence`, and they round-trip through the fold-seal codec. `ShardCoverage` stores the lexicographically minimal `{writer_epoch, build_sequence}` among live precommit bindings, stamps it on every Read visit, and carries it through Skip and durable fold-seal restart.

topic: Decoded PartManifest::entries must be strictly ascending by path
canonical_claim: Decoded `PartManifest::entries` must be strictly ascending by `path`; binary search and all index-free folder-view queries rely on this invariant. `decodePartManifest` rejects `path <= prev_path`; the encoder already emits sorted entries, and the strict ordering guarantee is what makes `PartFolderView` index-free.

topic: A same-manifest re-promote is allowed and must be
canonical_claim: A same-manifest re-promote is allowed and must be idempotent; the guard compares the existing manifest_ref with the manifest_ref being promoted rather than rejecting every already-committed ref. Build::promote proceeds when the target ref is absent or already names the same manifest_ref, and throws ABORTED when it names a different committed manifest_ref.; The promote-over-committed fix fails closed with `ABORTED` when `refs[final_ref_name]` names a different committed manifest, while `ContentAddressedTransaction::republishRef` is idempotent for a destination with the same path-sorted entries and throws `ABORTED` for different content.

topic: republishRef compares only the source and destination PartManifest
canonical_claim: republishRef compares only the source and destination PartManifest entries and drops the source ref without staging a new manifest when the entries match. republishRef determines idempotency from PartManifest::entries, not ManifestId, because a re-drive mints a new manifest ID for the same content. PartManifest::entries are canonical path-sorted vectors, so element-wise vector equality is stable for comparing source and destination content.; republishRef is idempotent when the destination is already committed with the same content; a different-content destination is an ABORTED conflict.

topic: A committed CAS repoint is implemented as the
canonical_claim: A committed CAS repoint is implemented as the existing `publishEntries` sequence plus an `allow_repoint` mode on `Build::promote`, matching the modeled TLA transition `WRepoint`. For a ref key `K`, `repointRef` maps to `WRepoint(mOld, mNew, ref=K, w)`: one journal event in one namespace carries `old=Bind(mOld)` and `new=Bind(mNew)` under the same ref. `Build::promote` accepts a trailing `bool allow_repoint = false`; when it is true and the committed ref names a different manifest, it emits one committed-transition RefOp from the current `ManifestRef` to the new `id.ref` and emits `CasEventType::RefRepoint`. `repointRef(const PartRefKey &, std::vector<Cas::ManifestEntry>, Cas::ProvenanceOp)` returns false and performs zero pool mutations or events when the candidate manifest is byte-equal to the committed manifest; otherwise it publishes with `allow_repoint=true`, increments `ProfileEvents::CasRefRepoint`, logs the ref and entry count at warning level, and erases the cached folder view on success.; A byte-equal repoint is a zero-mutation no-op with no audit event.; A byte-equal repoint performs zero pool mutations, including no manifest PUT and no ref-log record.

topic: Pool/CasRefLedger owns ref-table state and locks, ref transaction
canonical_claim: `Pool/CasRefLedger` owns ref-table state and locks, ref transaction allocation and queueing, recovery/seals, snapshot publication, stale-precommit sweeping, cache eviction, remount/shutdown coordination, and ref read/lifecycle entry points. `CasRefLedger` owns the ref-table map, ref-queue and per-table state mutexes, append/recovery/seal lanes, snapshot publication, stale-precommit sweep, cache eviction, remount coordination, and ref lifecycle/read entry points.

topic: RefCowMap consists of an immutable shared std::shared_ptr<const std::map<String
canonical_claim: `RefCowMap` consists of an immutable shared `std::shared_ptr<const std::map<String, RefCommittedRow>> base` and a per-copy `std::map<String, std::optional<RefCommittedRow>> overlay`, with present entries as overrides and `nullopt` as tombstones. `RefCowMap` copies share the immutable base and copy only the overlay, keyed reads check overlay before base, point writes modify overlay, ordered iteration merges both sorted ranges, and `materialize()` folds the overlay into a fresh base once per flush. `RefCowMap::materialize()` merges overlay values and tombstones into a new immutable base, then clears the overlay and resets `net_delta`. `RefCowMap` keyed access checks overlay entries first, treats tombstones as misses, writes only to overlay, and performs sorted two-range merge iteration for cold full scans. `RefCowMap::materialize()` is O(n) once per flush and restores `base + empty overlay`, so ordinary keyed reads between flushes access the base without merge overhead.; `RefCowMap::size()` and `empty()` are O(1) because `net_delta` tracks overlay inserts and tombstones relative to the immutable base size.

topic: Before the incremental-budget change, admits() fully rebuilt and
canonical_claim: Before the incremental-budget change, `admits()` fully rebuilt and encoded both a snapshot and a hypothetical whole-namespace removal transaction for every state-growing operation, making a K-op batch against N live refs cost O(K×N). The new `admits()` applies the candidate operation to a scratch state and compares `snapshotFramingSize + snapshot_body_bytes` and `removalFramingSize + removal_body_bytes` against the budgets, reducing a flush batch from O(K×N) to O(K) while preserving the existing preview identifiers and framing. The incremental `admits()` plan replaces the O(N)-per-operation full re-encode with two running body-byte totals on `RefTableState`, turning a K-op flush batch against an N-ref table from O(K×N) into O(K) with byte-identical decisions.; Before the incremental budget fix, `admits()` rebuilt and encoded the full ref table for each state-growing operation, scaling as O(N log N) with live ref count N; `BM_Admits` ranged from 48.8 microseconds at N=100 to 55,976 microseconds at N=100,000.

topic: The only row-population paths for RefTableState are stateFromSnapshot
canonical_claim: The only row-population paths for `RefTableState` are `stateFromSnapshot` and `applyOpInPlace`; these are therefore the only paths that seed or maintain the body-byte counters. The incremental-budget implementation maintains `snapshot_body_bytes` and `removal_body_bytes` at five row-mutation sites in `applyOpInPlace` and seeds them once in `stateFromSnapshot`.

topic: The size helpers committedRowEncodedSize, precommitRowEncodedSize, snapshotFramingSize, re
canonical_claim: The size helpers `committedRowEncodedSize`, `precommitRowEncodedSize`, `snapshotFramingSize`, `removalOpEncodedSize`, and `removalFramingSize` calculate sizes by using the same encoder fragments as the full formats, avoiding hand-written escaping or length arithmetic. The incremental-budget size helpers are factored from the existing snapshot and log encoders so per-row and framing sizes remain byte-identical to full encoding by construction.

topic: The incremental admits() change does not alter the
canonical_claim: The incremental `admits()` change does not alter the ref wire format or persisted data and needs no compatibility scaffolding because CAS is pre-release. The incremental-budget change must preserve the snapshot and removal transaction wire formats and requires no `NativeFormat` specification update.

topic: CasRefLedger::ensureRefTableRecovered retries the whole recovery attempt, including namesp
canonical_claim: `CasRefLedger::ensureRefTableRecovered` retries the whole recovery attempt, including namespace `LIST`, snapshot/log `GET`s, replay, and the seal `PUT`, rather than retrying only the seal. Each CAS ref-table recovery retry starts from a fresh `LIST`, and the recovery steps are idempotent because the seal uses a conditional `PUT` with a deterministic `seal_id` and resolves an already-landed identical seal as `Committed`.

topic: RefCowMap::find creates a non-mergeable base iterator for an
canonical_claim: `RefCowMap::find` creates a non-mergeable base iterator for an overlay-only key, so incrementing the iterator can skip later base entries even though the primitive is documented as a `std::map` replacement. `RefCowMap::find` builds a non-mergeable iterator for overlay-only keys by using `base->find(key)` instead of the sibling base branch's `lower_bound`; with base={A,D} and overlay-only B, `find("B")` then `++` hits a state bitwise equal to `end()` and silently skips D. Not reachable through current point-dereference-only callers, but the fix (`lower_bound`) is a strict improvement, identical when the key is shadowed.

topic: After encapsulation, RefTableState keeps lifecycle, transaction, committed-map, precommit
canonical_claim: After encapsulation, `RefTableState` keeps lifecycle, transaction, committed-map, precommit, and byte-counter storage private; external code reads through accessors and mutates state only through protocol entry points such as `applyRefLogTxn`, `replay`, `stateFromSnapshot`, and `admits`. `RefTableState` was encapsulated as a closed class with private fields and public getters; mutation is restricted to `applyRefLogTxn`, `replay`, `stateFromSnapshot`, and `materializeCommitted`.

topic: Recovery replay streams post-snapshot RefLogTxn objects one at
canonical_claim: Recovery replay streams post-snapshot `RefLogTxn` objects one at a time after sorting keys by transaction ID, reducing recovery memory to O(one transaction) regardless of tail length. Streaming ref recovery applies decoded transactions one at a time into a private candidate `RefTableState` and never mutates live `rt.state` until complete recovery is ready. The stage-1 `RefReplayBuilder` owns a private candidate, applies decoded transactions in place, discards it on failure, and returns a complete `RecoveryResult`; vanished objects re-list, while decode or apply corruption fails fast.

topic: An item with more than ref_txn_max_ops operations fails
canonical_claim: An item with more than `ref_txn_max_ops` operations fails alone, while removal-class items are exempt from the op cap only when their built operations contain `RemoveNamespace`; `WholeShard` scope alone is not the discriminator. CAS removal classification and chunking share the same op-inspection discriminator: production `RemoveNamespace` is `WholeShard`-scoped and singleton-carved, while normal chunks split before exceeding the operation cap.

topic: Ref transaction identifiers are allowed to have safe
canonical_claim: Ref transaction identifiers are allowed to have safe gaps: an append refused before any network attempt can leave a gap, so a missing id in an otherwise ordered sequence is not by itself evidence of incomplete enumeration. A missing sequence id is not itself anomalous because a pre-attempt refused append can leave a safe gap; an object that exists at or below the cursor but was never applied is the unambiguous anomaly.

topic: Within each (namespace, epoch), durable ref ids are
canonical_claim: Within each `(namespace, epoch)`, durable ref ids are dense from 1 through the greatest applied sequence, and the next id is `greatest_applied.ref_sequence + 1`; the pool-wide `next_ref_sequence` allocator is removed. `CasRefLedger::allocateRefTxnId` derives ids per namespace from `getGreatestApplied()`: `{E, greatest_applied.ref_sequence + 1}` in the same epoch, or `{E, 1}` after an epoch change; `next_ref_sequence` is deleted.

topic: After any writer-epoch transition, the first touch CAS-walks
canonical_claim: After any writer-epoch transition, the first touch CAS-walks the dead tail using the `slot-occupy` result states `Created`, `Occupied(bytes, token)`, and `Unresolved`; an occupied `EpochSeal` terminates the walk, while an occupied straggler is adopted and replayed. During recovery epoch transitions, `Created` closes an epoch, an occupied seal is adopted, an occupied non-seal straggler at `T+1` is applied and the seal is retried at the new `T+1`, and `Unresolved` enters transient retry; recovery never mints `T+2` blindly. The first recovery or touch after every writer-epoch transition, including a clean transition, must CAS-walk and seal the previous nonempty stream; an adopted EpochSeal terminates the walk.; A dedicated slot-occupy primitive should return Created, Occupied(GetResult), or Unresolved, preserve occupant bytes and token, decode an occupied RefLogTxn or EpochSeal, and terminate immediately when it adopts a seal.

topic: Checkpoint updates use one read-validate-merge-token-CAS algorithm for append
canonical_claim: Checkpoint updates use one read-validate-merge-token-CAS algorithm for append, snapshot publication, and sealing; identical merged bodies skip the CAS, and a contribution above `committed_through` is corruption. `publishCkpt` follows read, validate, merge, identical-body skip, and token-CAS; token conflicts retry only until the deadline, and every attempt reruns `checkFenceOrThrow(admitted_generation)` after its read and before its CAS. If merging proposed _ckpt fields produces the exact current body, the publisher must return without a same-bytes CAS; recovery or merge retries must use the existing recovery deadline and bounded-restart accounting.; Concurrent _ckpt publishers must use a read/decode/merge/CAS loop that takes the semantic maximum of pointer fields and preserves unrelated fields.

topic: The append order is immutable log PUT, _ckpt.committed_through
canonical_claim: The append order is immutable log PUT, `_ckpt.committed_through` CAS, in-memory install/acknowledge, and allocation of the next id; if the frontier publication is unresolved, the lane remains `NeedsRecovery` and returns no success. The ref durability order is `log PUT → _ckpt CAS → ack`, and retry-after-conflict must perform a whole-body exact re-read and re-merge regardless of the first-attempt `_ckpt` view policy.; The per-life `_ckpt` object carries `committed_through`, the exact acknowledged frontier, plus the checkpoint-snapshot pointer and seal chain; append order is log PUT, `_ckpt` CAS, then acknowledgement.

topic: The prev_epoch_seal field is populated by recovery seals
canonical_claim: The `prev_epoch_seal` field is populated by recovery seals and by every ordinary sequence-1 transaction after an epoch transition; recovery installs the chain's final seal in `RefTableRuntime::last_epoch_seal`. A namespace's genesis epoch is its life_epoch; last_epoch_seal is none exactly at genesis, and sequence 1 requires prev_epoch_seal iff writer_epoch > life_epoch; Recovery must install the exact last-seal identifier into the writer runtime, and commitRefChunk must copy it into every ordinary non-genesis sequence-1 transaction

topic: The _ckpt value is represented by RefCkpt{life_epoch, checkpoint_snapshot_id
canonical_claim: The `_ckpt` value is represented by `RefCkpt{life_epoch, checkpoint_snapshot_id, last_epoch_seal}` and both append and snapshot writers use the same `mergeCkpt` semantic-max helper. For incarnation-keyed `_ckpt`, joining an unknown `life_epoch` with `E` yields `E`, joining `E` with `E` yields `E`, and two different present `life_epoch` values in one incarnation are corruption rather than `max`; `checkpoint_snapshot_id` and `last_epoch_seal` still merge by semantic maximum.

topic: tryPublishSnapshotAndAdvanceCheckpointOnce must make the immutable snapshot body durable
canonical_claim: `tryPublishSnapshotAndAdvanceCheckpointOnce` must make the immutable snapshot body durable, advance `_ckpt`, and only then adopt the snapshot in memory; retry and backoff semantics remain unchanged. The three publication effects are ordered as durable snapshot body, advanced `_ckpt`, and in-memory adoption; `Poisoned` refuses publication and triggers re-recovery. CasRefLedger::trySnapshotPublishOnce must publish _ckpt after the snapshot body is durable and test its race, identical-body no-op, token conflict, and fence behavior through the real call site A normal snapshot publication writes the snapshot body before advancing the publisher checkpoint, and the body PUT and checkpoint CAS are each observed as one request for the publication attempt. Snapshot publication records the _snap body with ref_request_controller->putIfAbsentControlled(refSnapshotKey(...)) before calling publishCkptContribution(...); reversing that order makes the ordering test fail.; CasRefLedger::trySnapshotPublishOnce must invoke the shared publishCkpt helper after the snapshot body is durable and before treating the snapshot as cleanup-authoritative

topic: A permanent Retired catalog history grows with every
canonical_claim: A permanent `Retired` catalog history grows with every historical namespace and eventually makes legitimate admissions return `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`; normal `Atomic` UUID churn does not bound that history. An immortal `Retired` row makes the catalog `O(historical namespaces)` on the hot full-object CAS path and eventually exhausts the catalog's admission budget; exact compaction is unavailable for arbitrary opaque names.; The ref catalog is a single raw token-CAS object capped at 256 MiB; admission is checked against both the encoded catalog byte size and a separate per-entry fold-seal reservation. A permanent never-deleted `Retired` history would eventually exhaust this cap, returning `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` on new namespace admission regardless of live cardinality — the GET/decode/encode/whole-object-CAS cost also grows with total historical births, not current live count.

topic: Before its fix, Build::promote could overwrite an existing
canonical_claim: Before its fix, `Build::promote` could overwrite an existing committed `refs[R]` without emitting a removal for the old binding, leaving two committed owner bindings for `R` and permanently pinning the old manifest and uniquely-owned blobs. `Build::promote` overwrites `refs[R]` without emitting a committed-to-committed repoint event, so the previously committed manifest and its uniquely owned blobs remain pinned forever. `Build::promote` can overwrite an existing committed ref (`refs[dst]=T_a`) with a new manifest (`T_b`) without releasing `T_a`, permanently orphaning (leaking) the old manifest and its blobs; this is the most concrete confirmed storage leak from the review. Fix: `Build::promote` must, when `refs[R]` already names another manifest, either emit a proper committed-to-committed repoint or fail closed with an exception; also move `Build::abandon`'s `retireBuildSeq` call after the removal mutation.

topic: Treating a vanished catalog as an empty catalog
canonical_claim: Treating a vanished catalog as an empty catalog is unsafe: the retry path could replace every namespace's catalog with a single mutation's output via create-if-absent; `PoolMeta::admitOrValidate` is the fail-closed analogue. A retry path that treats a vanished CAS catalog object as an empty catalog is a silent-default-substitution defect: on retry after a vanish, it would replace every namespace's catalog with a single mutation's output via create-if-absent; the in-tree analogue `PoolMeta::admitOrValidate` already fails closed on exactly that observation and was cited as the pattern to follow.; Pool bootstrap must create the empty `cas/ref_catalog` before marking the Stage-B format ready, after which missing catalog reads cannot be treated as an empty catalog.; The mandatory catalog design treats an absent or undecodable `cas/ref_catalog` after pool initialization as `CORRUPTED_DATA` and stops creation, removal, and GC instead of interpreting it as a virgin empty catalog.
